The best universities for event management in the UK combine academic study with live projects, industry exposure, placement opportunities and practical event experience.

For 2027 entry, the University of Surrey, Sheffield Hallam University, Oxford Brookes University, the University of Westminster, the University of Greenwich, Cardiff Metropolitan University, Manchester Metropolitan University and Coventry University are among the strongest options to compare.

Quick Answer

If you want a short answer, start with Surrey for international event management, Sheffield Hallam for practical and professional training, Oxford Brookes for hands-on learning with a competitive confirmed 2027 fee, and Westminster for studying in central London.

Greenwich is particularly strong if you want events combined with innovation, while Cardiff Met offers live projects and internship opportunities. Manchester Met suits students who value industry networking in a major events city, and Coventry stands out for flexible start dates.

These are not ranked from first to eighth because the best university for event management depends on your course goals, preferred location, budget and the type of practical experience you want.

How We Chose These Universities

Calling a university one of the "best" should have a reason behind it.

We compared these universities using five practical factors:

  • Availability of a relevant event management course for 2027
  • Live projects, placements or other practical experience
  • Industry or professional connections
  • Entry requirements and course accessibility
  • Tuition fees, value and clarity of published applicant information

We also looked at how clearly each course fits common student searches for event management degrees in the UK, undergraduate study, international event management and postgraduate options.

The result is a focused shortlist rather than a long list created simply to reach ten universities.

Top Universities for Event Management in the UK for 2027

1. University of Surrey

Best for: International event management and repeated live-event experience

Course: BSc (Hons) International Event Management

Start: September 2027

Duration: 3 years, or 4 with Professional Training

Typical entry: BCC to CCC

2027 tuition: TBC

Planning estimate: UK £9,800 to £10,050; International £23,500 to £24,000

Placement: Professional Training route available

Surrey is one of the strongest choices for students interested specifically in international events.

Its BSc combines event planning and management with live projects, venue visits, industry interaction and opportunities to develop practical experience throughout the course. Students can also extend the degree by taking a Professional Training year.

Here is the thing. Practical experience is particularly valuable in events because the job rarely involves one skill at a time. You may need to manage suppliers, budgets, venues, audiences and unexpected operational problems within the same project.

Surrey's final 2027 tuition fee has not yet been published. The latest course fee provides the basis for the planning range above rather than being presented as a confirmed 2027 charge.

Check the official International Event Management course information before making a final financial decision.

2. Sheffield Hallam University

Best for: Practical training and professional qualifications

Course: BSc (Hons) Events Management

Start: September 2027

Duration: 3 years, or 4 with placement

Typical entry: 104 UCAS points

2027 tuition: UK £10,050; International/EU £18,900

Placement: Available

Professional edge: Licensing and health and safety training

Sheffield Hallam is particularly easy to compare because it already publishes clear 2027 information.

Students study event design and delivery alongside project management, leadership, people management, licensing and safety. The course also includes professional training associated with BIIAB and IOSH.

That combination makes Sheffield Hallam attractive if your priority is practical preparation rather than studying events mainly as a theoretical business subject.

The 2027 fees are also confirmed at £10,050 per year for UK students and £18,900 for international and EU students.

You can verify the figures and course structure on Sheffield Hallam's official 2027 Events Management course page.

3. Oxford Brookes University

Best for: Hands-on event experience with competitive confirmed 2027 fees

Course: BSc (Hons) Events Management

Duration: 3 years, or 4 with work placement

2027/28 tuition: UK £10,050; International £18,500

Placement: Available

Placement-year fee: £2,010 for 2027/28

Oxford Brookes strengthens this shortlist because it combines practical event learning with confirmed 2027 pricing.

Students can develop experience through event activity and industry-facing work while studying subjects connected to planning, operations, sustainability and professional event management.

The international tuition fee of £18,500 for 2027/28 also makes Oxford Brookes one of the lower confirmed international fee options in this comparison.

That does not automatically make it the best choice, but students comparing value as well as practical experience should take it seriously.

The current fees and programme details are available through the university's official Events Management course page.

4. University of Westminster

Best for: International events in central London

Course: BA (Hons) International Event Management

Start: September 2027

Duration: 3 years, or 4 with placement

Typical entry: BBC or 112 UCAS points

2027 tuition: UK £10,050; International £19,000

Location: Marylebone, central London

Westminster has an obvious advantage for students who want to study inside one of the UK's largest event markets.

Its International Event Management degree combines event management with sustainability, live client work, industry exposure and an international perspective.

The location also puts students close to venues, conference spaces, exhibitions, agencies and brand events across London.

For 2027, the annual tuition fee is confirmed at £10,050 for UK students and £19,000 for international students. Westminster also states that the international fee remains fixed during the course after enrolment.

Eligible students entering with certain EU qualifications may qualify for a £4,500 first-year tuition fee reduction under the university's current award scheme.

5. University of Greenwich

Best for: Event management, innovation and entrepreneurship

Course: BA (Hons) Events Management and Innovation

Typical entry: 112 UCAS points

Duration: 3 years full-time, or 4 years sandwich

2027 tuition: TBC

Planning estimate: UK about £10,050; International £18,500 to £19,000

Placement: Optional sandwich placement

Professional recognition: Institute of Event Management

Greenwich takes a slightly different approach from a conventional events degree.

Its programme combines event design and delivery with entrepreneurship, finance, digital marketing, leadership, festivals and live entertainment. Full-time students also gain practical experience by organising events during their studies.

The programme has recognition from the Institute of Event Management, giving students another useful connection to the professional events sector.

The final 2027/28 fee is still TBC, so the figure above should be used only for early financial planning.

The latest course structure and entry information can be checked on the university's official 2027 Events Management and Innovation page.

6. Cardiff Metropolitan University

Best for: Live projects and internship opportunities

Course: BA (Hons) Events Management

2027 entry: Available

Typical entry: 112 UCAS points

English requirement: IELTS 6.0 overall with at least 5.5 in each element where required

2027 tuition: TBC

Planning estimate: UK about £10,000; International £16,000 to £17,000

Experience: Live event projects and internship route

Cardiff Met deserves a place in the top eight because practical event activity sits at the centre of the degree.

Students can work on live projects and choose a route that includes an internship. That can be particularly useful if you want to leave university with more than academic assignments on your CV.

Its latest international undergraduate fee also suggests Cardiff Met may remain one of the more affordable options in this shortlist, although the final 2027 figure should be confirmed before applying.

This is a useful reminder that the most expensive course is not necessarily the best investment. Course fit and real experience can matter more.

See Cardiff Met's official 2027 Events Management course information for the latest details.

7. Manchester Metropolitan University

Best for: Industry networking in a major UK events city

Course: BA (Hons) Events Management

Start: September 2027

Typical entry: 104 to 112 UCAS points

English requirement: IELTS 6.0 overall with no element below 5.5 where required

2027 tuition: TBC

Planning estimate: UK about £10,050; International £20,000 to £21,000

Manchester has a large music, sport, entertainment, hospitality and conference economy. That gives an events degree a useful local setting.

Manchester Met's course covers event operations, safety, responsible event creation, technology, digital marketing and live event production.

Students can also meet professionals through industry activities and guest speakers.

For someone who wants to start building professional connections before graduation, that ecosystem can be as important as an extra module on the course specification.

The 2027 tuition fee remains TBC. Check the university's official September 2027 Events Management course page before budgeting your final costs.

8. Coventry University

Best for: Flexible start dates and applied event management

Course: BA (Hons) Events Management

2027 starts: September and November 2027, with further 2028 starts listed

Duration: 3 years full-time, or 4 years sandwich

Typical entry: 112 UCAS points

2027 tuition: TBC

Planning estimate: UK about £10,050; International £18,000 to £18,500

Placement: Professional placement or study-abroad options

Coventry offers one of the more flexible schedules in the shortlist.

The Events Management BA covers areas such as event experiences, marketing, PR, digital media and the impact of events. Students can also choose a sandwich route that adds professional experience.

Those applied modules make Coventry particularly relevant for students interested in areas such as corporate event management, event production and branded experiences.

The final 2027 fee is not yet confirmed. The planning range above uses the latest published fee as a baseline and allows for a modest increase.

Check the official 2027/28 Events Management course before making an application decision.

Event Management Degrees UK Universities Offer

Students searching for event management degrees UK universities provide will find several different course types.

Events Management BA or BSc

These are broad degrees covering planning, marketing, operations, budgeting and event delivery.

International Event Management

These courses place more emphasis on global audiences, international event environments and cross-border event business.

Events Management and Innovation

This route combines event planning with entrepreneurship, innovation and business development.

Marketing and Events Management

This type of course suits students who want to combine events with branding, campaigns, digital marketing and audience development.

Master's in Event Management

Postgraduate courses suit graduates who want specialist knowledge, a career change or progression into strategic roles.

Among universities with event management degrees, the exact title matters less than what you will study and what experience you can gain.

A placement can easily prove more valuable than a small difference in university ranking.

If you are still comparing subjects, look at other courses with strong demand in the UK before committing to one route.

Entry Requirements for Event Management Courses in the UK

Across the undergraduate universities in this guide, typical entry requirements sit around 104 to 112 UCAS points.

Surrey currently uses a BCC to CCC A-level offer instead.

International students must also meet country-specific academic requirements and any English-language conditions.

IELTS requirements on the courses reviewed commonly sit around 6.0 to 6.5, but there is no single requirement that applies to every university.

Before submitting an undergraduate application, make sure you understand how the UCAS process works and how English-language requirements vary between UK universities.

Event Management Tuition Fees and Study Costs in 2027

Three universities in this shortlist already have confirmed 2027 undergraduate tuition figures:

  • Sheffield Hallam: £10,050 UK; £18,900 international
  • Oxford Brookes: £10,050 UK; £18,500 international
  • Westminster: £10,050 UK; £19,000 international

For the full shortlist, a reasonable early planning range is:

  • UK undergraduate tuition: approximately £9,800 to £10,100 per year
  • International undergraduate tuition: approximately £16,000 to £24,000 per year
  • One-year specialist master's tuition: approximately £11,000 to £21,000 across the programmes compared here

These figures show why comparing only tuition can be misleading.

A London university may have a similar course fee to one elsewhere in the UK but considerably higher accommodation costs. On the other hand, a placement may allow you to gain paid experience and improve your CV.

Students trying to control costs should also compare UK universities with lower international tuition fees.

Which Is the Best University for Event Management?

The best university for event management depends on what you want from the degree.

Choose Surrey if international event management and repeated live-event experience are your priorities.

Choose Sheffield Hallam if you want practical training, professional qualifications and a placement route.

Choose Oxford Brookes if hands-on learning and a comparatively competitive confirmed 2027 international fee appeal to you.

Choose Westminster if you want to study in central London.

Choose Greenwich if innovation and entrepreneurship matter.

Choose Cardiff Met if live projects, an internship route and lower-cost planning are high priorities.

Choose Manchester Met if you want to build connections within Manchester's events sector.

Choose Coventry if flexible intakes and applied modules suit your plans.

Here is the counterintuitive part: a more expensive university is not automatically a better investment.

A course with stronger practical opportunities, a useful placement and modules that match your career plans may offer far more value.

International applicants who are still deciding whether the country itself is right for them can also review what studying in the UK involves for overseas students.

Careers After an Event Management Degree

Graduates can work across:

  • Corporate events
  • Conferences
  • Exhibitions
  • Festivals
  • Sport
  • Hospitality
  • Weddings
  • Charity events
  • Venue operations
  • Brand experiences

Typical job titles include event coordinator, event manager, venue manager, conference organiser, event marketing executive, festival producer and event operations manager.

The strongest degree programmes also give students concrete evidence to discuss at interview.

Delivering a live event, managing a budget, solving a venue problem or completing a professional placement tells an employer much more than simply saying you studied event management.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the top universities for event management in UK?

Strong 2027 options include Surrey, Sheffield Hallam, Oxford Brookes, Westminster, Greenwich, Cardiff Met, Manchester Met and Coventry. The best option depends on location, course content, practical experience, fees and placement opportunities.

Which universities offer event management degrees in the UK?

Many UK universities offer event management degrees. The eight compared here all provide dedicated event-focused courses rather than relying only on a small number of event modules inside a general business degree.

What are the best event management courses UK students can compare?

Surrey is strong for international event management, Sheffield Hallam for practical training, Oxford Brookes for hands-on study, Westminster for London, Greenwich for innovation, Cardiff Met for live projects, Manchester Met for industry networking and Coventry for flexible starts.

What is the best bachelor in event management?

There is no single answer. Surrey and Sheffield Hallam offer strong BSc options, while Westminster, Greenwich, Cardiff Met, Manchester Met and Coventry offer relevant BA routes. Oxford Brookes also offers a practical BSc Events Management degree.

What are the top universities for masters in event management?

Surrey, Oxford Brookes, Westminster and Greenwich are strong postgraduate options to compare. Look carefully at the programme content, fees, professional recognition and intended start date.

What are the best masters in event management in the UK?

The answer depends on your goals. Oxford Brookes offers Global Events Management, Surrey focuses on international events, Westminster offers Event Design and Management, while Greenwich provides an International Events Management route.

How much does an event management degree cost in the UK in 2027?

A useful planning range is around £9,800 to £10,100 per year for UK undergraduate tuition and approximately £16,000 to £24,000 per year for international undergraduate tuition across the universities reviewed here.

Is event management a BA or BSc degree?

It can be either. The modules, practical experience and placement options are more important than whether the final award is a BA or BSc.

Do event management degrees include placement years?

Several do. Surrey, Sheffield Hallam, Oxford Brookes, Westminster, Greenwich and Coventry all offer relevant placement or sandwich opportunities, subject to individual course conditions.

Can international students study event management in the UK?

Some universities may accept alternatives to IELTS, so applicants can also check UK study options that may accept other evidence of English.

Final Thoughts

The best universities for event management in the UK for 2027 are not simply the institutions with the biggest names or highest tuition fees.

Surrey, Sheffield Hallam, Oxford Brookes, Westminster, Greenwich, Cardiff Met, Manchester Met and Coventry all offer credible options, but they suit different students.

Start by comparing the course modules, practical work and placement structure. Then look at the confirmed or estimated tuition fee and the total cost of living in the city.

That approach gives you a far better chance of choosing the right degree than relying on a university name alone.

If you need help narrowing down your options, you can discuss your UK university shortlist with an adviser.
